blocks.title: Повторение урока 7: планы и прогнозы
paragraphs: Вспомним три способа говорить о будущем из прошлого урока.
rules: Present Continuous — договорённость: I'm flying to Rome on Friday.
be going to — намерение и прогноз по фактам: I'm going to learn Spanish. Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.
will — решение на ходу, обещание, прогноз; после if / when — Present Simple: If it rains, we'll stay at home.

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: Look at the sky! It ___ rain.
tasks.explanation: Прогноз по тому, что видим сейчас — be going to.

tasks.prompt: Впишите will или won't: — I can't carry this bag. — Don't worry, I ___ help you.
tasks.explanation: Решение в момент разговора — will.

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay at home.
tasks.explanation: После if — Present Simple: rains.

tasks.prompt: Впишите Present Continuous (leave): Our train ___ at 8 am tomorrow — I've already bought the tickets.
tasks.explanation: Договорённость с точным временем — Present Continuous: is leaving.

blocks.title: Разогрев: работа, о которой вы мечтаете
paragraphs: Обсудите с преподавателем по-английски (задание 1a–1c из учебника).
prompts: Talk about a job you would like to do and a job you would not like to do. Explain your answers.
How many jobs can you name in one minute?
Which jobs work long hours? Which need several years of training? Which deal with people every day? Which often work in a team?
blocks.sample: I would like to be a vet, because I love animals and I would like to help them. I wouldn't like to be a taxi driver, because the work is tiring and you sit in the car all day. Doctors work long hours and need many years of training. Shop assistants and waiters deal with people every day. Firefighters and footballers often work in a team.

blocks.title: Лексика: Work (Vocabulary Focus 5A)
paragraphs: Послушайте и повторите выражения о работе. Составьте с каждым предложение о себе или о человеке, которого вы знаете.
blocks.transcript:
1. They have a nice working environment. They have a lot of skills.
2. I work long hours. I work weekends. I work in a team.
3. You need several years of training. You need good qualifications. You need a university degree.
4. I deal with serious problems. I deal with people every day.
5. I earn a good salary.
6. I am self-employed.
7. I make important decisions.

blocks.title: Чтение: The Coolest Jobs
paragraphs: Прочитайте о четырёх «самых крутых» профессиях. Подумайте: какая из них подошла бы вам и почему?
blocks.text:
The Coolest Jobs

The job website Job Hunter asked people what they thought were the coolest jobs - the kind of jobs that don't seem like work at all because they're a lot of fun! Meet some of the people who do these jobs:
Megan was once an accountant and a banker. Now she's a private island caretaker.
Ethan was once a lawyer. Now he's a bed tester.
Greg was once a scientist. Now he's a chocolate taster.
Alisha was once an IT worker. Now she's a video game designer.

A. Chocolate taster
Good for: someone who is good at tasting and smelling food and giving a clear opinion.
Qualifications or training: none - companies will probably give you training when you start the job.
What they do: they try a lot of food to understand differences in the taste. They decide if it is good or bad quality, but they don't usually swallow the food.
Negative things: they sometimes taste some really bad food!

B. Video game designer
Good for: someone who is creative, has a good imagination, and is good at drawing.
Qualifications or training: a degree in art or design is necessary, and it's also a good idea to understand some computer programming language.
What they do: they create characters, stories and situations. They work together with computer programmers and other developers. Teamwork is important.
Negative things: it's difficult to find a job because lots of people want to do this. Sometimes people work for a few months with no pay before they are offered a job.

C. Private island caretaker
Good for: an independent person - someone who likes to be outside and loves the sea.
Qualifications or training: none - your boss will explain the things you'll be doing.
What they do: they make sure everything is always ready for the owners. They often do gardening and fix things that are broken.
Negative things: it can be very lonely, so it's good for someone who likes to spend a lot of time alone.

D. Bed tester
Good for: someone who likes a very relaxed life. If you don't like getting up in the morning, this is the job for you!
Qualifications or training: none - but companies may give you training in the kinds of things you need to do.
What they do: you spend the day resting or sleeping while the company changes conditions of the room - they make it hot or cold or they change the light. Then you write a review.
Negative things: it's not really a permanent job, and there's only work when companies or hotels want you.

blocks.title: Аудирование: Alisha, Jason и Megan рассказывают о своей работе
paragraphs: Послушайте трёх людей (Track 05.03). Выясните, почему им нравится их работа и что нужно, чтобы так работать.
blocks.transcript:
Alisha: This is such a cool job because I get to do the thing I love most every day. I wasn’t very good at school work, probably because I spent too much time gaming. But I was good at art and drawing. When I was about 16, I met someone who was already working as a video game designer, and he told me that it’s difficult to get a job – you have to have good exam results and a good degree. So I did an extra maths course at school, and I also learned some computer programming. This meant I got onto a degree course to study game design. After I graduated, it still took me a year to find my dream job. Before that, I had a boring job as an IT worker in a company that sold software for accountants. But it was worth the wait! I really enjoy creating characters and stories for games – it’s amazing fun.
Jason: I always wanted a job where I could teach people new things – practical things – not the kind of things you have to study. When I left school, I started learning how to be an electrician, but I didn’t like my boss. I tried being a plumber, but that was boring. Then I found out that I can mix teaching with the other thing I love doing in life: getting on my skateboard and going around town. I love that feeling of freedom as you move quickly and easily among people and cars. I started working as an instructor about five years ago. You don’t have to have a degree or other qualification, but I found a course and got a certificate. It’s important because there are a lot of safety things you need to think about when you’re an instructor. For example, my students can’t have a lesson if they aren’t wearing a helmet. It’s a really amazing job – really cool!
Megan: For a couple of years, I worked for a bank, first as an accountant and then in client services. But I hated my job – too much stress! Then I saw this advert for an amazing job – it was like an escape. So for the past year, I’ve lived alone on this island where it’s so peaceful and quiet. I love it. It’s not the kind of job that just anyone can do. You have to be the kind of person who likes being alone. And you have to be practical, you know, good at fixing things yourself. But you don’t need any experience or training. And another thing – every day is like a work day. You can’t really have a day off because there’s always something to do – some gardening or cleaning or something. But you don’t have to do the same thing every day – it’s always different. It’s so relaxing here, and the island is so beautiful.

blocks.title: Правило 1: must и have to — необходимость (Grammar 5A)
paragraphs: Must и have to имеют похожие значения. Must часто пишут в правилах; люди с властью (учитель, врач) говорят must в речи. Have to — когда говорим, что необходимо; это обычно для разговорной речи. У must нет прошедшего и будущего — их заменяет have to.
formulas:
must + V1: необходимо (правило)

All employees must wash their hands. · You must turn off your phone.
?  Must I fill in this form? (в вопросах чаще: Do I have to fill in…?)
После must — глагол без to: You must go. Не «must to go».

have to / has to + V1: необходимо

+  We have to work hard. · She has to leave early today.
?  Do nurses have to have a degree? — Yes, they do. / No, they don't.
?  Does he have to wear a uniform? — Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
Прошедшее: had to — Yesterday I had to wait for two hours. Будущее: will have to.
rules: must — часто в письменных правилах и в речи людей, у которых есть власть: Visitors must wash their hands.
have to — когда говорим, что необходимо; очень часто в разговорной речи: Doctors have to work very long hours.
У must нет прошедшего времени: вчера — had to: Yesterday I had to wait for two hours. Не «I musted».
В будущем — will have to: Next year you will have to pass an exam.
blocks.transcript: We have to work hard. She has to leave early today. They don’t have to play. He doesn’t have to work. Do nurses have to have a degree? Yes, they do. No they don’t. Does he have to wear a uniform? Yes, he does. No he doesn’t.

tasks.prompt: Выберите слово: Passengers ___ show their passports at the border.
tasks.explanation: После must — глагол без to и без окончания.

tasks.prompt: Впишите have to или has to: My sister ___ get up at 6 am on school days.
tasks.explanation: С подлежащим she — has to.

tasks.prompt: Впишите have to в прошедшем времени: Yesterday we ___ wait for two hours at the airport.
tasks.explanation: Прошедшее время от have to — had to.

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: Next year I ___ take the exam.
tasks.explanation: У must нет будущего — will have to.

tasks.prompt: В каком предложении ошибка?
options: I musted call my boss yesterday.
She has to wear a uniform.
optionValues: I musted call my boss yesterday.
She has to wear a uniform.
tasks.answer: I musted call my boss yesterday.
tasks.explanation: У must нет прошедшего времени: надо I had to call.

tasks.prompt: Впишите вспомогательное слово (do, does или did): ___ you have to get up early on Sundays?
tasks.explanation: Вопрос с have to строится с do / does: Do you have to…?

blocks.title: Правило 2: mustn't, don't have to, can и can't (Grammar 5A)
paragraphs: Mustn't и don't have to имеют очень разные значения: mustn't — «нельзя» (запрет, важно этого не делать), don't have to — «не нужно» (можно не делать). Can говорит, что что-то разрешено, can't — что не разрешено или невозможно, похоже на mustn't.
formulas:
mustn't + V1: нельзя

Students mustn't talk during exams. · You mustn't eat in here.
mustn't = must not.  Вопросы с must в современном английском встречаются редко.

don't / doesn't have to + V1: не нужно

Teachers don't have to wear a uniform. · He doesn't have to work because he's rich.
Прошедшее: didn't have to — Yesterday I didn't have to get up early.

can / can't + V1: можно и нельзя

You can take a one-hour lunch break. (разрешено)
You can't eat here. · Doctors can't relax for very long. (не разрешено / не получается)
?  Can I eat here? — Yes, you can. / No, you can't.
rules: mustn't — делать нельзя, это важно: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
don't have to — делать не нужно, но и не запрещено: You don't have to book a table, there are lots of free ones.
can — правило разрешает, can't — не разрешает: Visitors can't touch the animals.
Не переводите don't have to как «нельзя» — это самая частая ошибка.
blocks.transcript: Speaker 1: You can leave work early today. Speaker 2: The children can’t go outside alone. Speaker 1: Can I eat here? Speaker 2: Yes, you can. No you can’t.

tasks.prompt: Знак «No photos». Выберите вариант: You ___ take photos here.
tasks.explanation: Фотографировать запрещено — mustn't.

tasks.prompt: Вход бесплатный. Выберите вариант: You ___ pay to enter.
tasks.explanation: Платить не нужно — don't have to.

tasks.prompt: Впишите mustn't или don't have to: You ___ run in the corridor — it's dangerous.
tasks.explanation: Бегать нельзя — запрет.

tasks.prompt: Впишите mustn't или don't have to: It's Sunday, so I ___ get up early.
tasks.answer: don't have to, do not have to
tasks.explanation: Вставать рано не нужно — нет необходимости.

tasks.prompt: Какое предложение значит «Можно не приходить»?
tasks.explanation: Don't have to — «не обязательно».

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: In this office you ___ wear jeans on Fridays — it's allowed.
tasks.explanation: Разрешено — can.

blocks.title: Чтение: Planning a safe future career
paragraphs: Прочитайте статью о будущем профессий. Найдите в ней все прогнозы (will, won't, might, may) и скажите, где автор уверен, а где нет.
blocks.text:
Planning a safe future career

Choose your future career carefully - experts are predicting big changes in the jobs we'll do in the next 10 to 20 years. Some jobs might disappear, but others will become more important.

The Internet is having a big effect. People already choose to do a lot of their shopping online, so there won't be as many shops, and there won't be many jobs for shop assistants. Bank clerks and other bank employees might also lose their jobs, as people may stop using cash altogether.

Another job that might disappear is taxi drivers. In the future, it will become normal to travel in cars without a driver, including taxis. Also, there may not be as many jobs for builders as there are today. Soon, 3D printers will make complete parts of buildings in just a few hours, and they might one day make whole buildings.

So which jobs are safe?

Computer programmers - A hundred years ago, there were none, but now there are a lot of them. And there will be even more in the future because almost all jobs will need computers.
Carers - People will live longer, and we'll need carers to look after us in our old age.
Robot specialists - We will use robots for many everyday jobs, but they will need a team of human workers to support them - designers, developers, programmers and salespeople.
Solar and wind power engineers - Over the next 20 years, it will become more important to use clean energy. There are now 10 million jobs in this area, but by 2050 it might be 30 million.

And of course, we will still need actors and musicians to entertain us, lawyers to argue and politicians to make the big decisions.

There will be more jobs for them
optionValues: There won't be many jobs for them
There will be more jobs for them
tasks.answer: There won't be many jobs for them
tasks.explanation: There won't be as many shops, and there won't be many jobs for shop assistants.

tasks.prompt: Выберите ответ: Why might bank clerks lose their jobs?
tasks.explanation: Bank clerks might lose their jobs, as people may stop using cash altogether.

tasks.explanation: It will become normal to travel in cars without a driver.

tasks.prompt: Выберите ответ: Which job will have even more people in the future?
tasks.explanation: There will be even more computer programmers because almost all jobs will need computers.

tasks.explanation: They might one day make whole buildings — автор не уверен.

tasks.prompt: Выберите ответ: How many jobs in clean energy might there be by 2050?
tasks.explanation: There are now 10 million jobs in this area, but by 2050 it might be 30 million.

blocks.title: Правило 3: will и might — прогнозы (Grammar 5B)
paragraphs: Will и might используют для прогнозов о том, что, как мы ожидаем, случится. Will и won't показывают, что мы очень уверены, might и might not — что мы менее уверены. В разговоре прогноз обычно начинают с I think…, I don't think… или Do you think…?
formulas:
will и might + V1

I'll say something silly. · They won't give me the job. (мы уверены)
They might ask difficult questions. · I might not get the job. (мы не очень уверены)
I'm sure I'll… — можно добавлять перед will: I'm sure I'll learn a lot.

Как говорить о прогнозах

I think you'll get the job. · I think he might get the job.
I don't think I'll get the job. (не «I think I won't»)
Do you think we'll get the job? — I think so. / I don't think so.
rules: will — мы уверены: In 2050 people will use even more technology.
might — возможно (мы не уверены): I might become a pilot.
Отрицание: won't — «точно не», might not — «возможно, не»: I might not get the job.
После will и might — глагол без to: It might change. Не «might to change».
blocks.transcript: I think you’ll get the job. I think he might get the job. I don’t think I’ll get the job. Do you think we’ll get the job? I think so. I don’t think so. Do you think we might get the job? We might. We might not.

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: In the future, robots ___ do dangerous jobs. (мы уверены)
tasks.explanation: Уверенный прогноз — will.

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант: I'm not sure, but we ___ work four days a week in the future. (возможно)
tasks.explanation: Возможно — might + V1.

tasks.prompt: Впишите will или might («возможно»): I ___ get a job today — you never know!
tasks.explanation: Не уверены — might.

tasks.prompt: Впишите отрицание с might + глагол exist («возможно, не будут существовать»): Some jobs ___ in twenty years.
tasks.explanation: Возможно, не будет — might not + V1.

tasks.prompt: Какое предложение значит «Точно не случится»?
options: Robots will probably take all jobs.
optionValues: Robots will probably take all jobs.
tasks.explanation: won't — «точно нет».

tasks.prompt: Выберите вариант («я не думаю, что получу работу»): I ___ I'll get the job.
tasks.explanation: I don't think I'll get the job — отрицание ставят в первую часть, а не в will.

blocks.title: Аудирование: три человека на ярмарке вакансий
paragraphs: Послушайте три коротких интервью на ярмарке вакансий (Track 05.07). Кто говорит о будущем увереннее всех?
blocks.transcript:
Interviewer: Are you enjoying the careers fair?
Sara: It’s not bad. It’s good to meet people from different companies.
Interviewer: Are you looking for work at the moment?
Sara: Yes. But it won’t be easy to find a job I’ll enjoy. There just aren’t enough jobs – you have to take what you can find. I applied for a job this week but I don’t think I’ll get an interview. They won’t be interested in me, because I don’t have any experience.
Interviewer: Are you enjoying the fair today?
Marco: Yeah it’s great. I’m sure I’ll make some really useful contacts. There are people from some really interesting companies here.
Interviewer: And are you applying for jobs at the moment?
Marco: Yes. I don’t think it’ll take long to find work. You never know … I might get a job today! I know someone who found a job at an event like this last year.
Interviewer: Are you enjoying it today?
Kate: Yes it’s good. It’s useful because I’m not sure what kinds of jobs I’m interested in.
Interviewer: So are you looking for work at the moment?
Kate: Not yet. I’m still studying and then I’ll try to get some work experience when I finish my course. After that I can start looking for a job. I might not get my perfect job, because not many people do, straight out of university.
Interviewer: And how do you feel about that?
Kate: Well.. I just need to pay the bills, you know. I’m sure I’ll find some kind of work because I’m happy to do anything they’ll pay me for. I can work my way up. I’ve got time!

tasks.explanation: Marco: I'm sure I'll make some really useful contacts... I might get a job today!

tasks.explanation: I might get a job today! — Марко не уверен.

optionValues: try to get some work experience
tasks.answer: try to get some work experience
tasks.explanation: I'm still studying and then I'll try to get some work experience when I finish my course.

blocks.title: Произношение: звук /ʃ/ и ударение в словах урока
paragraphs: Звук /ʃ/ («ш») пишется по-разному. Послушайте слова (Track 05.12). Русская подсказка в скобках — приблизительное чтение; точные звуки показывает транскрипция.
formulas:
Звук /ʃ/ («ш») в разных написаниях

shop assistant /ʃɑːp əˈsɪstənt/ (шап эси́стэнт) — sh
musician /mjuˈzɪʃn/ (мьюзи́шн) · politician /ˌpɑːləˈtɪʃn/ (палити́шн) — ci, ti

Penny: Are you working this summer?

paragraphs: Прочитайте статью с советами. К каждому абзацу подберите проблему и подчеркните все советы (Turn on…, You should…, Don't use…).
blocks.text:
How to deal with life's little problems

You don't have any money, you never finish anything you start, your house is dirty, you can't find a good job and your whole life is terrible. Well, maybe it's not that bad! If you'd like to improve things, we can help. Here are our top ways to deal with some of life's little problems.

1. My home is a mess
Learn to enjoy cleaning and tidying. People who enjoy this usually have clean homes. Turn on the TV or listen to music while you clean. Start by cleaning every day, but only for 15 minutes. When the 15 minutes are finished, you should stop. Don't worry if things aren't perfectly clean. Do a little bit of cleaning every day, and in a week your place will look great.

2. I'm addicted to my phone
It's important to give yourself rules. When you go out with friends, decide how many times you will look at your phone - maybe only two or three times in an evening. Ask your friends about how they feel. If they have the same problem as you, put all of your phones together in a pile out of the way. That way, no one can look at their phone, and you can all enjoy each other's company.

3. I can't concentrate on my work
The machine we use so much for work - our computer - is the same machine we often use to have fun. So control how you use your computer. If your problem is that you check your email every five minutes, you can get apps that stop the Internet from working for a period of time you choose. Use this time to focus on your work. But you shouldn't work for hours without a break. Work for half an hour and then take a five-minute break. Rewards are really important, too. Have a snack or get some fresh air every hour or so.

4. I don't sleep well
First, think about your body. Exercising regularly will help you to fall asleep more easily. You should try to drink less coffee, and eat less fast food, too. These bad habits keep you awake. Don't use devices with bright screens (for example, your mobile phone) before you go to sleep. They make your brain think that it is daytime instead of night time. Read a book and drink a cup of warm milk or herbal tea in the evening. Then you'll feel ready for sleep.

blocks.title: Правило 1: Imperative и should — советы (Grammar 6A)
paragraphs: Повелительное наклонение (imperative) и should мы используем, чтобы дать совет: сказать, что, по нашему мнению, лучше или правильнее. Императив сильнее, чем should: он говорит человеку, что именно делать. Should мягче — это совет, а не указание.
formulas:
Imperative: V1 / Don't + V1

Try to get a good night's sleep. · Don't stay up late.
Императив даёт советы, предупреждения (Be careful!) и инструкции (Turn left!).
Без подлежащего: Take a break. Не «You take a break» (это уже не совет).

should / shouldn't + V1

You should get up early. · Children shouldn't eat a lot of sweets.
?  Should I stop eating sweets? — Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
I think you should… / I don't think you should… — вежливее, потому что говорит о нашем мнении.
Do you think I should say sorry? — Yes, I think so. / No, I don't think so.
rules: Imperative — прямой совет без подлежащего: Turn on the TV or listen to music while you clean.
should — мягкий совет, одинаков для всех лиц: You should try to drink less coffee.
Отрицание: Don't + V1 и shouldn't + V1: Don't use devices with bright screens. You shouldn't work for hours without a break.
После should — глагол без to: You should go. Не «should to go».

blocks.title: Аудирование: Rachel советует Annie
paragraphs: Annie узнала плохую новость на работе. Послушайте часть 2 разговора (Track 06.14): какие советы даёт ей Rachel?
blocks.transcript:
PART 2
Rachel: So, what happened when you talked to your boss? Did you ask when you’re going to lose your job? Or if it’s completely certain?
Annie: No, I didn’t say much. I was too upset.
Rachel: Of course you were.
Annie: I didn’t really ask anything. What do you think I should do?
Rachel: OK, well, I’d get all the details first.
Annie: Right.
Rachel: So I think you should speak to your boss again. Maybe there’ll be other jobs there.
Annie: I don’t think that’s a good idea. I don’t know if I want to stay. Lots of people are unhappy there. And I don’t think there are any other jobs, anyway.
Rachel: OK, but I think it’s a good idea to ask. You don’t know what she’ll say.
Annie: I suppose so.
Rachel: And why don’t you speak to some of the people you work with? Ask them what they’re doing?
Annie: Mmm, I don’t think I should do that. My boss told me not to talk to anyone else. Because other people are going to lose their jobs, too.
Rachel: Mmm. You work in marketing, right?
Annie: Yeah.
Rachel: Well, Mark works in marketing, too. His company’s often looking for new people.
Annie: Really? Do you think I should speak to him about it?
Rachel: Definitely. I’ll speak to him, too.
Annie: OK. Great.
Rachel: And I wouldn’t worry too much – changing jobs could be a good thing. You’ll have the chance to do something new.
Annie: Yeah – you’re right.

blocks.title: Правило 3: просим совета, даём совет, предлагаем помощь (Everyday English 6C, 5C)
paragraphs: Эти фразы нужны в разговоре: как попросить совет, как его дать мягко, как показать сочувствие и как предложить помощь или идею. Послушайте фразы (Track 06.17).
formulas:
Просим и даём советы (6C)

Asking: What do you think I should do? · Do you think I should speak to him about it?
Giving: I'd get all the details first. · I think you should speak to your boss again. · I think it's a good idea to ask. · I wouldn't worry too much.
Not agreeing: I don't think that's a good idea. · I suppose so. · I don't think I should do that. · You're right.

Показываем сочувствие (6C)

How awful. · That's terrible. · What a pity. · I'm really sorry to hear that. · That's a shame.

Предложения помощи и идеи (5C)

I'll finish things here, if you want. · Shall I finish off those flowers? · Would you like me to prepare some of the orders? · Do you want me to take out the rubbish?
Why don't you tell me what we need to do? · Why don't I deal with this? · How about taking her some flowers? · Maybe you should start on the other order. · You could start with that order.
rules: I think you should + V1 / I wouldn't + V1 — самые частые способы дать мягкий совет.
Why don't you + V1? — совет; Why don't I + V1? — предлагаю сделать что-то я.
Shall I + V1? / Would you like me to + V1? / Do you want me to + V1? — предложение помощи.
How about + -ing / существительное — идея: How about taking her some flowers?

tasks.prompt: Прочитайте сообщение и ответ и выберите ответ: What does Sevim want help with?
tasks.text:
Sevim's message:

Dear Eliza,
I think my reading and listening are all right for my level, but I'm worried about my speaking. I don't feel very relaxed when I speak English, and I want to improve. Do you have any ideas?
Thank you,
Sevim

Eliza's reply:

Hi Sevim,
Thanks for your message. I'm glad that you wrote to me for ideas.

I remember when I was learning Turkish, I felt embarrassed about speaking. I could remember a lot of words and I knew grammar rules, but speaking was difficult. I now feel a lot more relaxed about speaking, so here are some ideas that I've taken from my own experience.

First of all, don't worry about making mistakes. Other people will still understand you, and they probably won't notice your mistakes. Secondly, remember that the only way to learn to speak a language is by speaking it. Use every chance you get to speak. For example, it's a good idea to use only English in class and not speak to other students in Turkish. You should also try practising the new vocabulary and grammar we learn in class by repeating it at home.

Next, you should think about extra speaking practice outside the classroom. You can join a conversation group, such as the chat groups in the study centre. They are free to join. Finally, you can also practise speaking online. For instance, there are a lot of websites where you can find speaking partners from all around the world.

I hope this helps you, and please feel free to talk to me after class next week.
Best wishes,
Eliza
tasks.explanation: I'm worried about my speaking.
